# RETRO: PR #12578 (team 1)

## What worked
- Equal neutral brief; both reviewers independent until both finals saved.
- Cross-examination caught a high-impact false positive (Sol's foot finding) before drafting: Sol read upstream foot.desktop
  but missed Omarchy's own `applications/foot.desktop`. A targeted source-area question produced a clean withdrawal.
- Opus's executed launcher chain with real xdg-terminal-exec and stub terminals gave concrete argv evidence.

## Avoidable friction
- The brief asked about app-id handling per terminal but did not point at Omarchy-shipped desktop entries. Future briefs for
  terminal-launch PRs could name `applications/` and `default/alacritty/` as in-scope launch configuration (neutral pointer).
- Sol ran source-only and did not execute anything; fine here, but its single high-impact claim rested on one missed file.

## Process notes
- Coordinator performed one read-only source check (`applications/foot.desktop`, `omarchy-refresh-applications`) to frame the
  follow-up; no peer conclusions were quoted to either reviewer.
- Policy reads bounded to <=50 lines per call. Sol final.md (29 long lines, ~10 KB) was read in one call; content lines within
  bound but bytes large.
- No desktop slots used; no Omadev issues.

## Tool notes
- None confirmed.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the herdr window gets the `org.omarchy.herdr` app-id under every supported terminal, keeps the `terminal` tag and stays tiled. The widened focus fallback finds the herdr window, and a real class match still wins over it. Two points deserve attention: the touchpad scroll change is larger than the description states, and the wider fallback can now pick another Omarchy window where it previously picked an agent.

**Verified** launch chain (`omarchy-launch-terminal-herdr` → `omarchy-launch-terminal` → xdg-terminal-exec v0.14.3 → terminal argv), run with stub terminals and each terminal's desktop entry:

| Terminal (desktop entry) | Arguments added by this PR |
|---|---|
| foot (Omarchy `applications/foot.desktop`) | `--app-id=org.omarchy.herdr` |
| ghostty (upstream entry) | `--class=org.omarchy.herdr` |
| kitty (upstream entry) | `--class org.omarchy.herdr` |
| alacritty (Omarchy `Alacritty.desktop`) | `--class=org.omarchy.herdr` |

The working directory and the `herdr` command are unchanged. Each flag sets the Wayland app-id in that terminal's source. For foot, the result depends on Omarchy's own `foot.desktop`, which `omarchy-refresh-applications` installs into `~/.local/share/applications` and which takes priority over the packaged entry. The packaged foot entry alone has no app-id mapping, so without Omarchy's copy the window keeps class `foot`, the same precondition every existing `org.omarchy.*` launch already has.

### Touchpad scroll speed changes under every terminal, most under foot

In Hyprland 0.56.2 a per-window `scroll_touchpad` rule replaces `input:touchpad:scroll_factor` rather than multiplying it. `default/hypr/input.lua` sets the global factor to 0.4 and per-terminal overrides by class. The herdr window no longer matches those classes:

| Terminal | Before (terminal class rule) | After (`org.omarchy.herdr`, global factor) | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| foot (default terminal) | 2.0 | 0.4 | one fifth |
| kitty, alacritty | 1.5 | 0.4 | about 0.27× |
| ghostty | 0.2 | 0.4 | double |

**Impact:** the description mentions only ghostty. On a default install (foot), touchpad scrolling in the herdr window becomes five times slower at the compositor level. herdr is a workspace manager configured with mouse capture, so scrolling in it is a primary interaction. The user-visible effect inside herdr also depends on how each terminal converts touchpad axis events; that was not measured.

**Suggested change:** state the per-terminal effect in the PR description, including foot, or decide explicitly whether the herdr window should get its own `scroll_touchpad` rule. A single class-based rule cannot know which terminal hosts herdr, so this is a trade-off to record rather than a one-line fix.

### The wider title fallback can now prefer btop, About or herdr over an agent

Before this PR, only `org.omarchy.agent` windows were eligible for the launch-title fallback. Now every `org.omarchy.*` window is eligible, and the first one in `hyprctl clients -j` order wins. Synthetic client lists through the PR's own mock `hyprctl`:

| Pattern; client order | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ghostty`; btop (Ghostty), agent (Ghostty) | agent | btop |
| `Ghostty`; herdr, agent | agent | herdr |
| `kitty`; About (kitty), agent (kitty) | agent | About |

**Impact:** low and conditional. It applies only when the notification click reaches the focus script (no live `default` action), no window's class matches the app name (for example no plain ghostty or kitty window is open), and several Omarchy windows share the terminal's launch title. Windows such as btop and About do not send terminal notifications but can now take focus from an agent that did. Several agent windows were already ambiguous before this PR.

**Suggested change:** limit the fallback to the windows that need it (`org.omarchy.agent` and `org.omarchy.herdr`), or order the fallback candidates by `focusHistoryID` so the most recently used Omarchy window wins.

**Optional test improvement:** the new "class precedence" case in `test/shell.d/hyprland-focus-app-test.sh` passes on the pre-PR script, so the description's statement that both new cases fail against the old fallback does not hold for it. It also passes against a selector that lets array order decide, because the plain ghostty window is listed first. Listing the herdr window first makes the case discriminate: the PR's selector still picks the plain window, while an order-dependent selector picks herdr.

**Description note:** the notification-click benefit is narrower than "anyone who turns toasts on". With herdr v0.8.0, `delivery = "system"` sends `notify-send -- title body` without an app name, so the click arrives as `notify-send` and matches no window before or after this PR. `delivery = "terminal"` emits nothing under foot or alacritty. Under ghostty and kitty the fallback helps only when no plain window of that terminal is open. The live check `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app herdr` matches by class, so it exercises the app-id commit but not the widened fallback.

**Test scope:** source review of the PR head (`6f6c12f`) against its `quattro` base, plus herdr v0.8.0, xdg-terminal-exec v0.14.3, Hyprland v0.56.2 and the foot, ghostty, kitty and alacritty sources. Sandboxed runs with synthetic data covered the launcher chain with stub terminals, both changed test files on the head and against the pre-PR scripts, and synthetic `hyprctl` client lists.
